Uniform Stirling central-limit analysis, supplemented by Poisson large-deviation tails uniform in the Hermite index, justifies passing the maximum through the limit. The limiting profile is a Gaussian squared-density integral; its derivative has one unique detached positive maximum and, for b>sqrt(2), a central local maximum. The strictly positive envelope derivative D'(b)=2[h(b)-h(U_b+b)] proves a unique dominance swap, with exact endpoints established by Gaussian Mills bounds. The 471 numerical assertions corroborate but do not replace proof.
